Item 1A. Risk Factors

The Company's business, reputation, results of operations, financial condition, and stock price can be affected by numerous factors, many of which are beyond the Company's control. The risks described below represent the most significant risks the Company has identified as of the date of this report; the Company also faces additional risks that are not presently known or that the Company currently considers to be immaterial.

Macroeconomic and Geopolitical Risks. Adverse macroeconomic conditions, including slow growth, inflation, supply-chain disruption, currency volatility, and regional conflict, have in the past and could in the future materially harm the Company's business and financial results. The Company's products are sold in markets that have experienced softening consumer demand in recent quarters; while management currently believes demand has stabilized, there is no assurance that conditions will continue to improve.

Competitive Risks. The markets for the Company's products and services are highly competitive. The Company competes with companies that offer a wide variety of devices, software platforms, content services, and accessories, including new entrants that may pursue aggressive pricing or vertical integration strategies. Failure to differentiate the Company's offerings, including the integration of intelligence features and on-device computing, could erode market share.

Supply-Chain Risks. The Company's supply chain is geographically concentrated, with a significant share of manufacturing capacity located in a small number of countries. Disruption — whether from policy shifts, public-health events, labor disputes, or weather — can delay shipments and increase component costs. While the Company has been diversifying its manufacturing footprint, the transition is multi-year and involves substantial execution risk.

Regulatory and Legal Risks. The Company is subject to a range of regulatory regimes worldwide, including those governing privacy, security, content moderation, app distribution, antitrust, and product safety. New or changed rules could compel the Company to alter business practices, accept lower margins, or pay material fines. Several pending legal proceedings could have an adverse outcome.

Cybersecurity Risks. Cyber-attacks on the Company's systems, products, services, or supply chain could compromise customer data, harm the Company's reputation, and require expensive remediation. The Company invests substantially in defenses, but no defense is perfect.

Tax Risks. Changes to corporate-tax laws in jurisdictions where the Company operates, including initiatives related to global minimum taxation, could increase the Company's effective tax rate.

The Company continues to monitor these and other risks and to invest in mitigation. Management believes the Company's strong balance sheet, brand, integrated platform, and ecosystem position it well to manage these risks over the long term.

Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

The following discussion should be read together with the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

Overview

Fiscal 2023 was a year of disciplined execution against a softer macroeconomic backdrop. Total net sales declined modestly year-over-year, primarily reflecting unfavorable foreign-exchange movement and continued normalization in hardware demand following the pandemic-era surge. Services revenue continued to expand, reaching a new all-time record and a record number of paid subscriptions on the Company's platform.

Looking ahead, management expects services to continue to be a source of durable growth, and expects gross-margin expansion in fiscal 2024 driven by services mix, supply-chain efficiency, and the absence of certain prior-year headwinds. Based on the strong launch of the Company's newest product lineup and current visibility into customer demand, management is raising its prior internal expectations for next-fiscal-year revenue growth and now anticipates double-digit growth in Services and low-to-mid single-digit growth in total revenue, subject to macroeconomic conditions.

Results of Operations

Total net sales decreased 2.8% to $383.3 billion. Products net sales decreased 3.4% to $298.1 billion, primarily driven by lower net sales of iPhone and Mac, partially offset by higher net sales of Services. Services net sales increased 9.1% to $85.2 billion, reflecting growth in advertising, the App Store, cloud services, and payment services.

Gross margin increased to 44.1% from 43.3%, primarily driven by a favorable mix shift toward higher-margin Services revenue and lower commodity and freight costs, partially offset by foreign-exchange headwinds and product-mix effects within Products.

Operating expenses increased 4.5%, reflecting higher R&D investment, particularly in custom-silicon development and machine-learning infrastructure.

Liquidity and Capital Resources

The Company generated $110.5 billion of operating cash flow in fiscal 2023 and ended the year with $162.1 billion of cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities. The Company returned $99.0 billion to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

The Company believes its existing cash, marketable securities, and cash generated from operations will be sufficient to fund its operating, investing, and financing activities for the foreseeable future, including continued investment in R&D and a robust capital-return program.

Outlook

For the first quarter of fiscal 2024, management expects revenue to be similar to the year-ago quarter, with services growth continuing to outpace product growth. While macroeconomic uncertainty persists, management views the operational backdrop as gradually improving and is confident in the Company's ability to deliver attractive results to shareholders.
